evidence: The dependency-neutral CredentialStore port exposes closed provider-key, connector-token, signing-trust, and encryption-key-material kinds; strict scoped references; compare-and-swap records; bounded recoverable failure classes; and a short-lived mutable lease that clears its buffer on close.

The Windows adapter protects one random profile-vault root with current-user DPAPI using CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN and never machine scope. Per-secret filenames are opaque HMAC tokens, and scoped metadata plus material are authenticated with XChaCha20-Poly1305 before any plaintext is returned.

Production Core composition now lazily creates or retrieves its stable object-encryption key through that vault. Real restart tests scan every project file including SQLite, project export output, the support-bundle contract, record filenames/bytes, log projections, and the exact CLI option set to prove that the key, secret identifiers, and secret material do not cross those boundaries or process arguments.

Corrupt authenticated records and unavailable DPAPI authority produce bounded recoverable errors while retaining the only ciphertext authority. Audit publication fails closed before a secret is returned or written, and two independent processes converge on one create-or-compare-and-swap object key under the cross-process vault lock.

Six credential-adapter tests exercise real DPAPI create/read/restart, lease zeroing, opaque records, authenticated corruption, DPAPI unprotect failure and recovery, compare-and-swap conflicts, audit denial, concurrent process creation, production object encryption, leakage scans, and redirected authority handling where the platform token permits creation.

Two strict portable contract tests reject weaker user/machine scope, unauthenticated records, plaintext identifiers, missing audit/CAS/recovery obligations, and schema expansion. Eight envelope-upgrade tests prove the production provider supports encrypted v4 completion and preserves the verified legacy source across key, journal, fsync, rename, metadata, cancellation, and restart failures.
The complete security-local profile additionally passed all 27 security tests and the live dependency/license/vulnerability policy scan with zero blocking findings at the exact implementation commit.

ADR-0017 records the accepted Windows current-user DPAPI profile-vault decision, threat boundary, alternatives, authenticated envelope, opaque addressing, audit denial, cross-process CAS, recovery duties, platform consequences, and verification obligations. The ADR registry and architecture checks pass.

The strict security contract schema/profile and documentation bind current-user scope, no plaintext persistence or process arguments, closed secret kinds and purposes, opaque locators, XChaCha20-Poly1305 records, CAS, content-free auditing, recoverable unavailable/corrupt outcomes, and zeroed bounded leases. No SQLite migration is appropriate because the accepted design explicitly forbids secret storage or vault locators in project databases.

The Core service and local-storage architecture documents explain production composition and the S03 handoff. Frozen build authority, package tests, build-input inventory, quality scope, and ADR tests include the new contract and modules. No UI reference, remote service, cloud deployment, connector implementation, key rotation workflow, or unrelated capability behavior was introduced.

The task claim, immutable build evidence, and generated planning views are the only non-implementation delta from the task base; W1 remains bound to the pre-Wave approval commit and CAP-02.S03.T02 is the completed dependency.
